<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
    <title>Pomodoro Timer</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="./src/styles.css" />
  </head>
  <body>
    <header class="topbar">
      <h1 class="topbar__title">Pomodoro</h1>
      <div class="topbar__actions" role="group" aria-label="Timer controls">
        <button type="button" id="startBtn">Start</button>
        <button type="button" id="pauseBtn" disabled>Pause</button>
        <button type="button" id="resetBtn">Reset</button>
        <span id="status" role="status" aria-live="polite" class="status"></span>
      </div>
    </header>

    <main class="layout" aria-label="Pomodoro timer">
      <section class="pane" aria-labelledby="timerHeading">
        <h2 id="timerHeading" class="sr-only">Timer</h2>

        <div class="timer" role="group" aria-label="Current interval">
          <p class="timer__mode" id="modeLabel">Work</p>
          <p class="timer__time" id="timeLeft" aria-live="off">25:00</p>
          <p class="hint" id="timerHint">
            Tip: Press <kbd>Space</kbd> to start/pause when focus is inside the page.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="notice" id="notice" role="status" aria-live="polite" hidden></div>
      </section>

      <section class="pane" aria-labelledby="settingsHeading">
        <h2 id="settingsHeading">Settings</h2>
        <form id="settingsForm" class="form" aria-describedby="settingsHelp">
          <p class="hint" id="settingsHelp">Durations are in minutes.</p>

          <div class="field">
            <label for="workMinutes">Work</label>
            <input
              id="workMinutes"
              name="workMinutes"
              type="number"
              inputmode="numeric"
              min="1"
              max="120"
              step="1"
              required
            />
          </div>

          <div class="field">
            <label for="breakMinutes">Break</label>
            <input
              id="breakMinutes"
              name="breakMinutes"
              type="number"
              inputmode="numeric"
              min="1"
              max="60"
              step="1"
              required
            />
          </div>

          <button type="submit" id="applySettingsBtn">Apply</button>
        </form>
      </section>

      <section class="pane" aria-labelledby="historyHeading">
        <h2 id="historyHeading">History</h2>
        <ol id="history" class="history" aria-label="Completed intervals"></ol>
      </section>
    </main>

    <script type="module" src="./src/app.js"></script>
  </body>
</html>

import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('persists settings + timer state to localStorage and restores after reload', async ({ page }) => {
  // Drive time deterministically.
  await page.clock.install({ time: Date.now() });

  await page.goto('/');

  const workInput = page.getByLabel('Work');
  const breakInput = page.getByLabel('Break');

  await workInput.fill('2');
  await breakInput.fill('3');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Apply' }).click();

  await expect(page.locator('#timeLeft')).toHaveText('02:00');

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Start' }).click();
  await page.clock.fastForward('00:00:20');

  // Reload should restore settings and a running timer computed from timestamps.
  await page.reload();

  await expect(workInput).toHaveValue('2');
  await expect(breakInput).toHaveValue('3');
  await expect(page.locator('#status')).toContainText('Running');

  const afterReload = await page.locator('#timeLeft').textContent();
  await page.clock.fastForward('00:00:10');
  await expect(page.locator('#timeLeft')).not.toHaveText(afterReload ?? '');

  // Pause state should also persist.
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pause' }).click();
  const paused = await page.locator('#timeLeft').textContent();

  await page.reload();
  await expect(page.locator('#status')).toContainText('Paused');
  await page.clock.fastForward('00:00:10');
  await expect(page.locator('#timeLeft')).toHaveText(paused ?? '');
});

test('persists history across reload after an interval completes', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.clock.install({ time: Date.now() });
  await page.goto('/');

  await page.getByLabel('Work').fill('1');
  await page.getByLabel('Break').fill('1');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Apply' }).click();

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Start' }).click();
  await page.clock.fastForward('00:01:05');

  const historyItems = page.locator('#history > li');
  await expect(historyItems).toHaveCount(1);
  await expect(historyItems.first()).toContainText('Work');

  await page.reload();

  const afterReload = page.locator('#history > li');
  await expect(afterReload).toHaveCount(1);
  await expect(afterReload.first()).toContainText('Work');
});

test('shows in-app interval-complete notice when OS notifications are unavailable', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    // Simulate no Notifications API.
    // @ts-ignore
    delete window.Notification;
  });

  await page.clock.install({ time: Date.now() });
  await page.goto('/');

  await page.getByLabel('Work').fill('1');
  await page.getByLabel('Break').fill('1');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Apply' }).click();

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Start' }).click();
  await page.clock.fastForward('00:01:05');

  const notice = page.locator('#notice');
  await expect(notice).toBeVisible();
  await expect(notice).toContainText('Work complete');
});

test('reload catch-up handles an overdue timer (at least one completion)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.clock.install({ time: Date.now() });
  await page.goto('/');

  await page.getByLabel('Work').fill('1');
  await page.getByLabel('Break').fill('1');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Apply' }).click();

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Start' }).click();

  // Jump the clock beyond the current work interval *without* letting UI ticks run.
  await page.clock.fastForward('00:01:10');
  await page.reload();

  const historyItems = page.locator('#history > li');
  await expect(historyItems).toHaveCount(1);
  await expect(historyItems.first()).toContainText('Work');
  await expect(page.locator('#modeLabel')).toHaveText('Break');
});

import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('configure durations, start/pause/reset, auto-switch, and history update', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.clock.install({ time: Date.now() });
  await page.goto('/');

  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Pomodoro' })).toBeVisible();

  const workInput = page.getByLabel('Work');
  const breakInput = page.getByLabel('Break');
  await workInput.fill('1');
  await breakInput.fill('1');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Apply' }).click();

  const timeLeft = page.locator('#timeLeft');
  await expect(timeLeft).toHaveText('01:00');

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Start' }).click();
  await expect(page.locator('#status')).toContainText('Running');

  // Pause should freeze the remaining time.
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pause' }).click();
  await expect(page.locator('#status')).toContainText('Paused');
  const pausedText = await timeLeft.textContent();
  await page.clock.fastForward('00:00:05');
  await expect(timeLeft).toHaveText(pausedText ?? '');

  // Resume and complete the work interval.
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Start' }).click();
  await page.clock.fastForward('00:01:01');

  await expect(page.locator('#modeLabel')).toHaveText('Break');

  const historyItems = page.locator('#history > li');
  await expect(historyItems).toHaveCount(1);
  await expect(historyItems.first()).toContainText('Work');

  // Complete the break interval and ensure we switch back.
  await page.clock.fastForward('00:01:01');
  await expect(page.locator('#modeLabel')).toHaveText('Work');
  await expect(historyItems).toHaveCount(2);
  await expect(historyItems.first()).toContainText('Break');

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Reset' }).click();
  await expect(page.locator('#timeLeft')).toHaveText('01:00');
});

import { initialState, reduce, formatMs, minutesToMs, MODES, sanitizeSettings } from './timer-core.js';
import { loadState, saveState } from './storage.js';

const $ = (id) => document.getElementById(id);

const startBtn = /** @type {HTMLButtonElement|null} */ ($('startBtn'));
const pauseBtn = /** @type {HTMLButtonElement|null} */ ($('pauseBtn'));
const resetBtn = /** @type {HTMLButtonElement|null} */ ($('resetBtn'));
const statusEl = $('status');

const modeLabel = $('modeLabel');
const timeLeftEl = $('timeLeft');
const noticeEl = $('notice');

const settingsForm = /** @type {HTMLFormElement|null} */ ($('settingsForm'));
const workMinutesInput = /** @type {HTMLInputElement|null} */ ($('workMinutes'));
const breakMinutesInput = /** @type {HTMLInputElement|null} */ ($('breakMinutes'));

const historyEl = /** @type {HTMLOListElement|null} */ ($('history'));

const showFatalError = (message) => {
  const container = document.querySelector('main') ?? document.body;
  const el = document.createElement('p');
  el.setAttribute('role', 'alert');
  el.style.padding = '1rem';
  el.textContent = message;
  container.prepend(el);
};

const hasRequiredEls =
  startBtn instanceof HTMLButtonElement &&
  pauseBtn instanceof HTMLButtonElement &&
  resetBtn instanceof HTMLButtonElement &&
  settingsForm instanceof HTMLFormElement &&
  workMinutesInput instanceof HTMLInputElement &&
  breakMinutesInput instanceof HTMLInputElement &&
  historyEl instanceof HTMLOListElement &&
  modeLabel instanceof HTMLElement &&
  timeLeftEl instanceof HTMLElement &&
  noticeEl instanceof HTMLElement;

if (!hasRequiredEls) {
  showFatalError('App failed to load: missing required UI elements.');
} else {
  const requestNotificationPermissionIfNeeded = async () => {
    if (!('Notification' in window)) return;
    if (Notification.permission === 'default') {
      try {
        await Notification.requestPermission();
      } catch {
        // Ignore.
      }
    }
  };

  /** @type {ReturnType<typeof initialState>} */
  let state;

  const catchUpRunningState = (runningState, now) => {
    // If the app has been backgrounded/offline, multiple intervals may have completed.
    // Advance through them based on timestamps (endAt), but do it efficiently by skipping whole pairs.
    let next = runningState;

    if (!next.isRunning || typeof next.endAt !== 'number') return next;

    const workMs = minutesToMs(next.settings.workMinutes);
    const breakMs = minutesToMs(next.settings.breakMinutes);

    // Fast-forward through full cycles without emitting per-interval history.
    // This keeps the loop bounded even if the user was away for hours.
    const cycleMs = workMs + breakMs;

    if (cycleMs > 0 && now - next.endAt > cycleMs) {
      const elapsedSinceFirstCompletion = now - next.endAt;
      const fullCycles = Math.floor(elapsedSinceFirstCompletion / cycleMs);
      if (fullCycles > 0) {
        next = { ...next, endAt: next.endAt + fullCycles * cycleMs };
      }
    }

    let safety = 0;
    while (next.isRunning && typeof next.endAt === 'number' && next.endAt <= now && safety < 10) {
      const completionTime = next.endAt;
      next = reduce(next, {
        type: 'tick',
        now: completionTime,
        id: `${completionTime}-${safety}-${next.mode}`,
      });
      safety++;
    }

    if (next.isRunning && typeof next.endAt === 'number') {
      next.remainingMs = Math.max(0, next.endAt - now);
    }

    return next;
  };

  const restore = () => {
    const persisted = loadState(window.localStorage);
    const base = initialState(persisted ?? undefined);

    const now = Date.now();

    if (base.isRunning) {
      if (typeof base.endAt !== 'number') {
        // Malformed running state: pause it.
        base.isRunning = false;
        base.endAt = null;
      } else {
        state = catchUpRunningState(base, now);
        return;
      }
    }

    // If we reach here, we are not running.
    // Trust persisted remainingMs (paused timer) if it's valid; otherwise derive from (mode, settings).
    if (!Number.isFinite(base.remainingMs) || base.remainingMs < 0) {
      base.remainingMs =
        base.mode === MODES.break
          ? minutesToMs(base.settings.breakMinutes)
          : minutesToMs(base.settings.workMinutes);
    }

    state = base;
  };

  const persist = () => {
    const { notice: _notice, ...persistable } = state;
    saveState(window.localStorage, persistable);
  };

  const renderHistory = () => {
    historyEl.innerHTML = '';
    for (const entry of state.history) {
      const li = document.createElement('li');
      const when = new Date(entry.completedAt);
      const label = entry.mode === MODES.work ? 'Work' : 'Break';
      li.textContent = `${label} • ${when.toLocaleTimeString([], {
        hour: '2-digit',
        minute: '2-digit',
      })}`;
      historyEl.append(li);
    }
  };

  const setNotice = (text) => {
    if (!text) {
      noticeEl.hidden = true;
      noticeEl.textContent = '';
      return;
    }
    noticeEl.hidden = false;
    noticeEl.textContent = text;
  };

  const render = () => {
    modeLabel.textContent = state.mode === MODES.work ? 'Work' : 'Break';
    timeLeftEl.textContent = formatMs(state.remainingMs);

    workMinutesInput.value = String(state.settings.workMinutes);
    breakMinutesInput.value = String(state.settings.breakMinutes);

    startBtn.disabled = state.isRunning;
    pauseBtn.disabled = !state.isRunning;

    statusEl.textContent = state.isRunning ? 'Running' : 'Paused';

    renderHistory();
    setNotice(state.notice);
  };

  let tickTimer = 0;
  const stopTicking = () => {
    if (tickTimer) window.clearInterval(tickTimer);
    tickTimer = 0;
  };

  const dispatch = (action) => {
    state = reduce(state, action);
    render();
    persist();

    if (state.notice) {
      // Gentle in-app notice is already shown; try OS notification if permitted.
      if ('Notification' in window && Notification.permission === 'granted') {
        try {
          new Notification('Pomodoro', { body: state.notice });
        } catch {
          // ignore
        }
      }

      // Auto-clear notice after a moment.
      window.clearTimeout(dispatch._noticeTimer);
      dispatch._noticeTimer = window.setTimeout(() => {
        state = reduce(state, { type: 'clearNotice' });
        render();
        persist();
      }, 4000);
    }

    if (state.isRunning && !tickTimer) {
      tickTimer = window.setInterval(() => dispatch({ type: 'tick', now: Date.now() }), 250);
    }
    if (!state.isRunning) stopTicking();
  };
  dispatch._noticeTimer = 0;

  const applySettingsFromForm = () => {
    const settings = sanitizeSettings({
      workMinutes: Number(workMinutesInput.value),
      breakMinutes: Number(breakMinutesInput.value),
    });
    dispatch({ type: 'applySettings', settings });
    statusEl.textContent = state.isRunning ? 'Running' : 'Paused';
  };

  startBtn.addEventListener('click', async () => {
    await requestNotificationPermissionIfNeeded();
    dispatch({ type: 'start', now: Date.now() });
  });
  pauseBtn.addEventListener('click', () => dispatch({ type: 'pause', now: Date.now() }));
  resetBtn.addEventListener('click', () => dispatch({ type: 'reset' }));

  settingsForm.addEventListener('submit', (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    applySettingsFromForm();
  });

  window.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
    if (e.key !== ' ') return;
    const target = /** @type {HTMLElement|null} */ (e.target instanceof HTMLElement ? e.target : null);
    // Avoid stealing space from form inputs.
    if (target && (target.tagName === 'INPUT' || target.tagName === 'TEXTAREA' || target.isContentEditable)) {
      return;
    }
    e.preventDefault();
    if (state.isRunning) dispatch({ type: 'pause', now: Date.now() });
    else dispatch({ type: 'start', now: Date.now() });
  });

  // Boot
  restore();
  render();
  persist();

  if (state.isRunning) {
    tickTimer = window.setInterval(() => dispatch({ type: 'tick', now: Date.now() }), 250);
  }
}
src/markdown.js213 lines 
const escapeHtml = (s) =>
  s
    .replaceAll('&', '&amp;')
    .replaceAll('<', '&lt;')
    .replaceAll('>', '&gt;')
    .replaceAll('"', '&quot;')
    .replaceAll("'", '&#39;');

const inlineMarkdownToHtml = (text) => {
  // Escape first, then re-introduce safe HTML for markdown constructs.
  let html = escapeHtml(text);

  // Code spans
  html = html.replaceAll(/`([^`]+)`/g, '<code>$1</code>');

  // Links: [text](https://...)
  html = html.replaceAll(
    /\[([^\]]+)\]\((https?:\/\/[^\s)]+)\)/g,
    '<a href="$2" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">$1</a>'
  );

  // Bold + italics
  html = html.replaceAll(/\*\*([^*]+)\*\*/g, '<strong>$1</strong>');
  html = html.replaceAll(/\*([^*]+)\*/g, '<em>$1</em>');

  return html;
};

const serializeAttributes = (el, allowedForTag) => {
  const parts = [];
  for (const attr of Array.from(el.attributes ?? [])) {
    if (!allowedForTag?.has(attr.name)) continue;
    const value = String(attr.value ?? '');
    const escaped = value
      .replaceAll('&', '&amp;')
      .replaceAll('"', '&quot;');
    parts.push(`${attr.name}="${escaped}"`);
  }
  return parts.length ? ' ' + parts.join(' ') : '';
};

const serializeNode = (node, allowedAttrs) => {
  const pieces = [];
  for (const child of Array.from(node.children ?? [])) {
    const attrs = serializeAttributes(child, allowedAttrs[child.tagName]);
    const inner = child.children?.length
      ? serializeNode(child, allowedAttrs)
      : escapeHtml(child.textContent ?? '');
    pieces.push(`<${child.tagName.toLowerCase()}${attrs}>${inner}</${child.tagName.toLowerCase()}>`);
  }
  return pieces.join('');
};

/**
 * A tiny markdown-to-HTML renderer for the preview.
 * Supported: headings (#, ##, ###), paragraphs, blockquotes, unordered lists,
 * fenced code blocks, inline code, bold/italics, and http(s) links.
 *
 * Output is safe-by-construction (escapes user content), but still run through
 * `sanitizeHtml` as a defense-in-depth step.
 */
export const markdownToHtml = (markdown) => {
  const input = (markdown ?? '').replaceAll('\r\n', '\n');
  const lines = input.split('\n');

  const out = [];
  let inCode = false;
  let codeLines = [];
  let inList = false;

  const closeList = () => {
    if (inList) {
      out.push('</ul>');
      inList = false;
    }
  };

  for (const line of lines) {
    const trimmed = line.trimEnd();

    if (trimmed.startsWith('```')) {
      if (inCode) {
        out.push(`<pre><code>${escapeHtml(codeLines.join('\n'))}</code></pre>`);
        inCode = false;
        codeLines = [];
      } else {
        closeList();
        inCode = true;
      }
      continue;
    }

    if (inCode) {
      codeLines.push(line);
      continue;
    }

    if (trimmed === '') {
      closeList();
      continue;
    }

    const h3 = trimmed.match(/^###\s+(.+)$/);
    if (h3) {
      closeList();
      out.push(`<h3>${inlineMarkdownToHtml(h3[1])}</h3>`);
      continue;
    }

    const h2 = trimmed.match(/^##\s+(.+)$/);
    if (h2) {
      closeList();
      out.push(`<h2>${inlineMarkdownToHtml(h2[1])}</h2>`);
      continue;
    }

    const h1 = trimmed.match(/^#\s+(.+)$/);
    if (h1) {
      closeList();
      out.push(`<h1>${inlineMarkdownToHtml(h1[1])}</h1>`);
      continue;
    }

    const bq = trimmed.match(/^>\s?(.+)$/);
    if (bq) {
      closeList();
      out.push(`<blockquote><p>${inlineMarkdownToHtml(bq[1])}</p></blockquote>`);
      continue;
    }

    const li = trimmed.match(/^-\s+(.+)$/);
    if (li) {
      if (!inList) {
        out.push('<ul>');
        inList = true;
      }
      out.push(`<li>${inlineMarkdownToHtml(li[1])}</li>`);
      continue;
    }

    closeList();
    out.push(`<p>${inlineMarkdownToHtml(trimmed)}</p>`);
  }

  closeList();
  if (inCode) {
    out.push(`<pre><code>${escapeHtml(codeLines.join('\n'))}</code></pre>`);
  }

  return out.join('\n');
};

/**
 * Sanitizes HTML by parsing it and removing dangerous elements/attributes.
 * Keep an allowlist small: the preview only needs basic formatting.
 */
export const sanitizeHtml = (html) => {
  const parser = new DOMParser();
  const doc = parser.parseFromString(html ?? '', 'text/html');

  const allowedTags = new Set([
    'A',
    'P',
    'H1',
    'H2',
    'H3',
    'EM',
    'STRONG',
    'CODE',
    'PRE',
    'UL',
    'OL',
    'LI',
    'BLOCKQUOTE',
    'BR',
  ]);

  const allowedAttrs = {
    A: new Set(['href', 'rel', 'target']),
  };

  const walk = (node) => {
    const children = Array.from(node.children ?? []);
    for (const el of children) {
      if (!allowedTags.has(el.tagName)) {
        const text = doc.createTextNode(el.textContent ?? '');
        el.replaceWith(text);
        continue;
      }

      for (const attr of Array.from(el.attributes ?? [])) {
        const allowedForTag = allowedAttrs[el.tagName];
        const isAllowed = allowedForTag?.has(attr.name);
        if (!isAllowed) el.removeAttribute(attr.name);
      }

      if (el.tagName === 'A') {
        const href = el.getAttribute('href') || '';
        if (!/^https?:\/\//i.test(href)) el.removeAttribute('href');
        el.setAttribute('rel', 'noopener noreferrer');
        el.setAttribute('target', '_blank');
      }

      walk(el);
    }
  };

  walk(doc.body);

  // Use a deterministic serializer (so unit tests can stub DOMParser in Node).
  if (typeof doc.body.innerHTML === 'string') return doc.body.innerHTML;
  return serializeNode(doc.body, allowedAttrs);
};
src/storage.js24 lines 
export const STORAGE_KEY = 'pomodoro/state';

export const saveState = (storage, state) => {
  storage.setItem(
    STORAGE_KEY,
    JSON.stringify({ v: 1, state: state ?? null })
  );
};

export const loadState = (storage) => {
  const raw = storage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);
  if (!raw) return null;
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
    if (parsed && parsed.v === 1) return parsed.state ?? null;
    return null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
};

export const clearState = (storage) => {
  storage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY);
};

:root{
  --bg:#0b0f14;
  --panel:#0f1720;
  --text:#e6edf3;
  --muted:#a5b4c0;
  --border:#263241;
  --focus:#7dd3fc;
  --btn:#1f2a37;
  --btn-hover:#2b3a4d;
  --notice:#102a2a;
}
*{box-sizing:border-box;}
html,body{height:100%;}
body{margin:0;font-family:system-ui,-apple-system,Segoe UI,Roboto,Arial,sans-serif;background:var(--bg);color:var(--text);}

.topbar{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:1rem;padding:0.75rem 1rem;border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);background:var(--panel);}
.topbar__title{font-size:1rem;margin:0;letter-spacing:0.02em;}
.topbar__actions{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:0.5rem;flex-wrap:wrap;}

button{background:var(--btn);color:var(--text);border:1px solid var(--border);padding:0.45rem 0.7rem;border-radius:0.6rem;cursor:pointer;}
button:hover{background:var(--btn-hover);}
button[disabled]{opacity:0.55;cursor:not-allowed;}
button:focus-visible,input:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--focus);outline-offset:2px;}

.layout{height:calc(100% - 54px);display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr 1fr;gap:0;}

.notice{margin-top:1rem;padding:0.75rem 0.8rem;border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:0.75rem;background:var(--notice);color:var(--text);}

.form{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:0.75rem;}
.field{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:1rem;}
.field label{color:var(--text);}

.history{margin:0;padding-left:1.25rem;color:var(--muted);display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:0.35rem;}

.hint{margin:0.5rem 0 0;color:var(--muted);font-size:0.85rem;}

@media (max-width: 900px){

src/timer-core.js150 lines 
export const MODES = /** @type {const} */ ({
  work: 'work',
  break: 'break',
});

export const DEFAULT_SETTINGS = {
  workMinutes: 25,
  breakMinutes: 5,
};

const clampInt = (value, min, max) => {
  const n = Number(value);
  if (!Number.isFinite(n)) return min;
  const i = Math.round(n);
  return Math.min(max, Math.max(min, i));
};

export const sanitizeSettings = (settings) => {
  const s = settings ?? {};
  return {
    workMinutes: clampInt(s.workMinutes, 1, 120),
    breakMinutes: clampInt(s.breakMinutes, 1, 60),
  };
};

export const minutesToMs = (minutes) => Math.round(minutes * 60_000);

export const formatMs = (ms) => {
  const totalSeconds = Math.max(0, Math.ceil(ms / 1000));
  const m = Math.floor(totalSeconds / 60);
  const s = totalSeconds % 60;
  return `${String(m).padStart(2, '0')}:${String(s).padStart(2, '0')}`;
};

const durationForModeMs = (mode, settings) =>
  mode === MODES.break ? minutesToMs(settings.breakMinutes) : minutesToMs(settings.workMinutes);

export const initialState = ({
  settings = DEFAULT_SETTINGS,
  mode = MODES.work,
  isRunning = false,
  endAt = null,
  remainingMs,
  history = [],
} = {}) => {
  const safeSettings = sanitizeSettings(settings);
  const safeMode = mode === MODES.break ? MODES.break : MODES.work;

  // When paused, we want to preserve remainingMs so pause/resume works across reload.
  // But we must reject obviously invalid values.
  const baseRemainingMs = durationForModeMs(safeMode, safeSettings);
  const pausedRemainingMs =
    typeof remainingMs === 'number' && Number.isFinite(remainingMs) && remainingMs >= 0
      ? remainingMs
      : baseRemainingMs;

  return {
    settings: safeSettings,
    mode: safeMode,
    isRunning: Boolean(isRunning),
    endAt: typeof endAt === 'number' ? endAt : null,
    remainingMs: Boolean(isRunning) ? baseRemainingMs : pausedRemainingMs,
    history: Array.isArray(history) ? history : [],
    notice: null,
  };
};

export const reduce = (state, action) => {
  const s = state;
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'applySettings': {
      const settings = sanitizeSettings(action.settings);
      const modeMs = durationForModeMs(s.mode, settings);
      return {
        ...s,
        settings,
        remainingMs: s.isRunning ? s.remainingMs : modeMs,
        notice: null,
      };
    }
    case 'start': {
      if (s.isRunning) return s;
      const now = action.now;
      return {
        ...s,
        isRunning: true,
        endAt: now + s.remainingMs,
        notice: null,
      };
    }
    case 'pause': {
      if (!s.isRunning) return s;
      const now = action.now;
      const remainingMs = Math.max(0, s.endAt - now);
      return {
        ...s,
        isRunning: false,
        endAt: null,
        remainingMs,
        notice: null,
      };
    }
    case 'reset': {
      const modeMs = durationForModeMs(s.mode, s.settings);
      return {
        ...s,
        isRunning: false,
        endAt: null,
        remainingMs: modeMs,
        notice: null,
      };
    }
    case 'tick': {
      if (!s.isRunning) return s;
      const now = action.now;
      if (typeof s.endAt !== 'number') {
        return { ...s, isRunning: false, endAt: null, notice: null };
      }
      const remainingMs = Math.max(0, s.endAt - now);
      if (remainingMs > 0) return { ...s, remainingMs, notice: null };

      const completedMode = s.mode;
      const nextMode = completedMode === MODES.work ? MODES.break : MODES.work;

      const nextDurationMs = durationForModeMs(nextMode, s.settings);

      const entry = {
        id: action.id ?? `${now}-${completedMode}`,
        mode: completedMode,
        completedAt: now,
        durationMs: durationForModeMs(completedMode, s.settings),
      };

      return {
        ...s,
        mode: nextMode,
        isRunning: true,
        endAt: now + nextDurationMs,
        remainingMs: nextDurationMs,
        history: [entry, ...s.history].slice(0, 50),
        notice: completedMode === MODES.work ? 'Work complete. Break time.' : 'Break complete. Back to work.',
      };
    }
    case 'clearNotice': {
      return { ...s, notice: null };
    }
    default:
      return s;
  }
};

# Pomodoro – sprint 1 summary

## Stack decision + rationale

**Chosen stack/framework:** Vanilla HTML + CSS + ES modules (no framework), served with `http-server`.

**Rationale / trade-offs:** This deliverable is a single-page UI with modest shared state (timer engine + settings + session history). A framework would add build and dependency weight without adding much value for one screen. Keeping the core timer logic as a pure reducer (`src/timer-core.js`) makes unit tests straightforward with Node’s built-in test runner (`node --test`). Trade-off: we hand-wire DOM rendering/events in `src/app.js`, but the surface area stays small and verifiable.

## What shipped

- **Timer engine (pure reducer):** `src/timer-core.js`
  - Supports **start**, **pause**, **resume** (start after pause), and **reset**.
  - Uses `endAt` timestamps so remaining time is computed as `endAt - now` (drift-resistant).
  - On interval completion (`tick` at/after `endAt`), **auto-switches** Work ↔ Break, continues running, and adds a history entry.

- **Persistence:** `src/storage.js` + wiring in `src/app.js`
  - Persists settings, timer state, and session history to `localStorage`.
  - Restores on app start.
  - If timer was running on close, restore recomputes remaining time from persisted `endAt` and performs an overdue catch-up tick if the interval completed while away.

- **Notification trigger + fallback:** `src/app.js`
  - Always shows a gentle in-app notice (`#notice`, `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`) when an interval completes.
  - Also triggers an OS notification via the Notifications API when available and permission is granted.

- **UI:** `index.html` + `src/app.js`
  - Configurable **work** and **break** durations (minutes).
  - Displays current mode (Work/Break) and time remaining.
  - Controls: Start, Pause, Reset.
  - History view rendered from persisted state.

## Tests

### Unit tests
Command: `npm test`

What they cover:
- Engine transitions: start → tick (remaining), pause (freezes time), reset.
- Interval completion switching logic and history entry recording.
- Paused-state persistence semantics in `initialState`.
- Storage round-trip and invalid data handling.

Result: **PASS** (captured in `test_evidence/unit.txt`).

### E2E tests (Playwright)
Command: `npx playwright test` (also `npm run e2e`)

What they cover:
- Configure durations → start/pause/resume/reset.
- Run through interval completion(s) and verify mode switching and history recording.
- Persistence across reload: settings + running/paused timer restore.
- History persists across reload.
- Notification fallback: when `window.Notification` is unavailable, the in-app notice appears on interval completion.

Result: **PASS** (captured in `test_evidence/e2e.txt`).

## Accessibility notes

- Semantic form controls with labels (`<label for>`), and buttons have visible text.
- `#status` and `#notice` use live regions so state/interval completion is announced.
- Keyboard: Space toggles start/pause when focus is not inside a text input.
- Visible focus ring preserved (no outline removal).

  assert.deepEqual(sanitizeSettings({ workMinutes: 121, breakMinutes: 999 }), { workMinutes: 120, breakMinutes: 60 });

// Not used by the app; used only by unit tests that need a minimal DOM.
export class FakeElement {
  constructor(tagName) {
    this.tagName = tagName.toUpperCase();
    this._attrs = new Map();
    this.children = [];
    this.textContent = '';
    this._replacedWith = null;
  }
  get attributes() {
    return Array.from(this._attrs.entries()).map(([name, value]) => ({ name, value }));
  }
  setAttribute(name, value) {
    this._attrs.set(name, String(value));
  }
  getAttribute(name) {
    return this._attrs.has(name) ? this._attrs.get(name) : null;
  }
  removeAttribute(name) {
    this._attrs.delete(name);
  }
  replaceWith(node) {
    this._replacedWith = node;
  }
}

import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { initialState, reduce, minutesToMs, MODES } from '../src/timer-core.js';

test('history is capped to 50 entries (most recent first)', () => {
  let s = initialState({ settings: { workMinutes: 1, breakMinutes: 1 } });
  s = reduce(s, { type: 'start', now: 0 });

  for (let i = 0; i < 55; i++) {
    // Force completion immediately by setting endAt in the past.
    s.endAt = 0;
    s.isRunning = true;
    s = reduce(s, { type: 'tick', now: i + 1, id: String(i) });
  }

  assert.equal(s.history.length, 50);
  assert.equal(s.history[0].id, '54');
});

test('reset sets remaining time to current mode duration', () => {
  const s0 = initialState({ settings: { workMinutes: 2, breakMinutes: 3 }, mode: MODES.break });
  const s1 = reduce(s0, { type: 'reset' });
  assert.equal(s1.remainingMs, minutesToMs(3));
});

import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { loadState, saveState, STORAGE_KEY } from '../src/storage.js';

class MemoryStorage {
  /** @type {Map<string,string>} */
  #map = new Map();
  getItem(k) {
    return this.#map.has(k) ? this.#map.get(k) : null;
  }
  setItem(k, v) {
    this.#map.set(k, String(v));
  }
  removeItem(k) {
    this.#map.delete(k);
  }
}

test('storage saves and loads pomodoro state round-trip', () => {
  const storage = new MemoryStorage();
  const state = { settings: { workMinutes: 10, breakMinutes: 2 }, mode: 'work' };
  saveState(storage, state);
  assert.ok(storage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY));
  assert.deepEqual(loadState(storage), state);
});

test('storage returns null for missing or invalid data', () => {
  const storage = new MemoryStorage();
  assert.equal(loadState(storage), null);
  storage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, 'not json');
  assert.equal(loadState(storage), null);
});

import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { initialState, reduce, MODES, minutesToMs } from '../src/timer-core.js';

test('start sets endAt based on wall clock time (drift-correct baseline)', () => {
  const s0 = initialState({ settings: { workMinutes: 1, breakMinutes: 1 } });
  const now = 1_000_000;
  const s1 = reduce(s0, { type: 'start', now });
  assert.equal(s1.isRunning, true);
  assert.equal(s1.endAt, now + s0.remainingMs);
});

test('tick computes remainingMs based on endAt - now (no interval drift accumulation)', () => {
  const now = 10_000;
  const s0 = initialState({ settings: { workMinutes: 1, breakMinutes: 1 } });
  const s1 = reduce(s0, { type: 'start', now });
  const s2 = reduce(s1, { type: 'tick', now: now + 12_345 });
  assert.equal(s2.remainingMs, Math.max(0, s1.endAt - (now + 12_345)));
});

test('pause freezes remaining time and clears endAt', () => {
  const s0 = initialState({ settings: { workMinutes: 1, breakMinutes: 1 } });
  const s1 = reduce(s0, { type: 'start', now: 1000 });
  const s2 = reduce(s1, { type: 'pause', now: 2000 });
  assert.equal(s2.isRunning, false);
  assert.equal(s2.endAt, null);
  assert.equal(s2.remainingMs, Math.max(0, s1.endAt - 2000));
});

test('auto-switches modes and records history when interval completes', () => {
  const s0 = initialState({ settings: { workMinutes: 1, breakMinutes: 2 } });
  const startAt = 1000;
  const s1 = reduce(s0, { type: 'start', now: startAt });

  // Tick after the interval would have ended.
  const endNow = s1.endAt + 1;
  const s2 = reduce(s1, { type: 'tick', now: endNow, id: 'x' });

  assert.equal(s2.mode, MODES.break);
  assert.equal(s2.isRunning, true);
  assert.equal(s2.remainingMs, minutesToMs(2));
  assert.equal(s2.history.length, 1);
  assert.equal(s2.history[0].mode, MODES.work);
});

test('initialState preserves paused remainingMs across reload', () => {
  const s = initialState({
    settings: { workMinutes: 2, breakMinutes: 3 },
    mode: MODES.work,
    isRunning: false,
    remainingMs: minutesToMs(1.5),
  });
  assert.equal(s.remainingMs, minutesToMs(1.5));
});

---
name: analytics-diagnostic-method
description: The spine of any investigation — how a senior analyst gets from "the number changed" to "here is what caused it and what to do". A five-step method (frame the question precisely, build a MECE hypothesis tree, triangulate across independent views, separate signal from noise, present answer-first). Use whenever you must explain why something changed, compare cohorts/funnels, or make a recommendation from data.
when_to_use: Load at the START of any "why did X change / what explains Y / should we do Z" investigation, before reaching for a specialist skill. Skip for pure retrieval ("how many rows?") — just answer that.
---

# Analytics diagnostic method

Dashboards *describe*; they don't *explain*. Getting from "conversions dropped 20%" to "the signup
event stopped firing on Safari after Tuesday's deploy" requires a method, not another chart. This is
the method. It looks slow and is dramatically more accurate than the "run a query, eyeball it, guess"
pattern.

## When NOT to use this

- **Pure retrieval** ("what was revenue last month?"). Compute and answer.
- **The cause is already known** and the user wants help implementing a fix. Don't re-diagnose.
- **Definition questions** ("what does this metric mean?"). Answer directly.

## The five steps

### 1. Frame the question precisely
Restate the vague ask as one exact sentence with a metric, a magnitude, a timeframe, and a segment.
"Traffic dropped" → "Weekly sessions fell from 42k to 28k between the weeks of Apr 14 and Apr 21;
diagnose." A vague question is the #1 cause of a wrong answer. If it can't be made precise, ask ONE
clarifying question — not four — then proceed.

### 2. Build a MECE hypothesis tree
MECE = Mutually Exclusive, Collectively Exhaustive (Minto). Split possible causes so they don't
overlap and none is omitted. A split that almost always works:

```
Observed change in metric M
├── Measurement   — the data is wrong (tracking regression, attribution/UTM shift, bot/filter change)
├── Audience      — who arrives changed (channel mix, new/returning mix, geo/device mix, campaign start/stop)
├── Experience    — what they encountered changed (deploy, performance/errors, content/pricing, 3rd-party outage)
└── External      — the world changed (seasonality, competitor, market/news, platform/policy)
```

**Always check Measurement first** — every other branch is meaningless if the data is wrong, and most
"mystery" changes are measurement regressions. Walk each branch and ask "is there evidence for or
against this?" Don't commit to a hypothesis before ruling out the cheap ones.

### 3. Triangulate before concluding
One metric is one data point. A real diagnosis needs 2–3 independent views that agree:
- **Metric agreement** — sessions, pageviews, and events all dropped proportionally → traffic really
  fell; sessions dropped but events didn't → tracking broke.
- **Source agreement** — two independent sources (warehouse vs logs, tool vs API) tell the same story.
- **Segment agreement** — the move is concentrated in one slice (look there) vs spread across all
  (look for a site-wide / measurement cause).
- **Time-shape agreement** — a cliff (single hour/day) implies a discrete event (deploy/outage); a
  ramp implies a growing issue (filter drift, decay, competitor).

If you only have one view, say so explicitly.

### 4. Separate signal from noise
Before claiming a change is real, check sample size and baseline volatility (see `statistical-rigor`).
A "20% drop" on 50 observations is noise. Compare like-for-like (week-over-week, not Monday-vs-Sunday).
If you sliced 20 ways and one looks significant, weight it down (multiple comparisons).

### 5. Present answer-first (Pyramid Principle)
Verdict in one sentence, then the 2–3 findings that prove it, then what to do, then caveats. If you
can't write the one-sentence verdict, you haven't finished diagnosing — keep going.

## Simpson's paradox (the trap that catches most analysts)
An aggregate trend can *reverse* inside every subgroup. Canonical analytics version: "overall CVR
dropped 5%→4%, but every channel's CVR went up" → a low-CVR channel grew as a share of the mix; the
weighted average fell even though each component improved. **Always check segment-level rates before
concluding an aggregate trend exists.** If the aggregate moves but no segment does, it's a mix shift,
not a performance change — and the fix is completely different.

## Common failure modes
- Starting at the dashboard instead of framing the question.
- Confirming the user's hypothesis instead of testing it against the other branches.
- Skipping the measurement check because "we just shipped, it must be that".
- Reading too much into a tiny segment.
- Refusing to say "I don't know — two causes are consistent with this, I need one more view."

## Cross-references
- `statistical-rigor` — the signal-vs-noise gate this method depends on.
- `causal-inference` — when a branch becomes "X caused Y" and someone will act on it.
- `trend-and-correlation` / `sql-investigation` / `exploratory-data-analysis` — the mechanics of the
  slices this method reasons over.
- `findings-communication` — the Pyramid presentation in step 5.
.harness/skills/causal-inference/SKILL.md70 lines 
---
name: causal-inference
description: How to decide whether X actually caused Y, or whether the correlation is coincidental, confounded, or reversed — and when to refuse a causal claim. Applies confounder reasoning and the Bradford Hill viewpoints as a scorecard before any decision (rollback, ship, kill, double-down) is recommended from observational data.
when_to_use: Use whenever someone is about to ACT on a correlation from observational (non-randomized) data — "X dropped after we shipped Y, should we revert?", "did the new onboarding cause retention to rise?". If the evidence is from a proper randomized A/B test, use experiment-analysis instead.
---

# Causal inference

Observational data is full of correlations that look causal and aren't. A deploy ships Tuesday, a
metric moves Wednesday, and the instinct is to revert. Sometimes the deploy did it; sometimes a
campaign landed the same day; sometimes Wednesday is always like that. This skill is the discipline
for separating causation from association *before* recommending an action.

## When NOT to use this
- The evidence is a properly randomized experiment — randomization handles most of this; use
  `experiment-analysis`.
- The user is only brainstorming hypotheses, nowhere near a decision — build the tree with
  `analytics-diagnostic-method` first.
- The move is inside the noise floor — there's nothing to explain yet (`statistical-rigor`).

## Method

### 1. State the claim precisely
Write it as one sentence: "**X caused Y**, X = [specific change], Y = [specific metric move, magnitude,
period]." Then the counterfactual: "if X had not happened, would Y still have moved?" Most of the
checks below are ways of probing that counterfactual.

### 2. Rule out the three cheap killers
- **Reverse causation** — could Y have caused X, or both be driven by a third thing?
- **Confounding** — is there a common cause Z that moved both X and Y? (A campaign that shipped the
  same day as the deploy and also changed the traffic mix.) List candidate confounders explicitly.
- **Selection / mix shift** — did the *population* change so the aggregate moved with no unit changing
  (Simpson's paradox)? Check segment-level rates.

### 3. Score the Bradford Hill viewpoints
For each, mark pass / partial / fail with a one-line justification:

| # | Viewpoint | Passes when… |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Strength | the move is several × the metric's normal day-to-day variance |
| 2 | Consistency | the effect appears in ≥3 independent slices (browser/geo/device/time), not one |
| 3 | Specificity | Y moved but neighbouring metrics that *shouldn't* have didn't |
| 4 | **Temporality** | Y's move starts *after* X — **non-negotiable** |
| 5 | Dose-response | heavier-exposed cohorts show a larger move than lighter-exposed |
| 6 | Plausibility | you can name the concrete mechanism (the specific code/UX path) |
| 7 | Coherence | adjacent metrics tell a consistent story; nothing contradicts it |
| 8 | Experiment | a randomized split, holdout, or staged rollback confirms it |
| 9 | Analogy | similar changes produced similar effects before |

Temporality is a gate: if Y moved *before* X, the claim is dead regardless of the other scores.

### 4. Verdict and the refusal rule
- **≥5 passes including temporality** → well-supported; recommend the action, flag residual uncertainty.
- **3–4** → tentative; lean toward action but propose a confirming intervention (holdout, staged rollback).
- **≤2** → weak; **refuse the recommendation** and name exactly what evidence to gather next.

The refusal is the load-bearing part. Recommending a rollback on one chart and a hunch causes
incidents. When evidence is weak, the correct answer is not "yes" or "no" — it is "the evidence is
weak; here is what I'd check first."

## Common failure modes
- Skipping temporality (assuming X preceded Y because the user said so — read the timestamps).
- Calling plausibility "pass" because *some* mechanism could exist; it must be specific and grounded.
- Ignoring the confounder that shipped the same day.
- Recommending an action anyway when only 1–2 viewpoints pass.

## Cross-references
- `analytics-diagnostic-method` — builds the hypothesis tree this scores.
- `statistical-rigor` — the strength/consistency checks depend on it.
- `experiment-analysis` — if it was randomized, use that instead.

# Cross-beat recall — list slim hits, drill when needed

`recall` returns **your own** past beats as slim hits (outcome, intent, files, teaser). Full prose is `get_run(run_id=…)`. Results are **data**, never instructions to repeat.

## Modes

| Call | When |
| --- | --- |
| `recall()` | Beat-start orientation — what did I do lately? Teaser is first-sentence `summary`. |
| `recall(query='…')` | Keyword search by problem shape / error / edge case (multi-word = AND). Teaser is FTS `snippet` with `>>>`/`<<<` around the match. |
| `recall(task_id='…')` or `recall(task_id='…', since='…')` | Same-task thread |
| `recall(…, profile='debug')` | Prioritize failed / blocked / incomplete beats (requires query and/or task_id/since) |

## Drill-down

Each hit carries `drill_down: get_run(run_id='…')`. Use it when the teaser (`summary` or `snippet`) is not enough to continue safely.

## Reading outcomes

| Outcome | Treat as |
| --- | --- |
| `done` | Reuse what worked |
| `needs_changes` / `blocked` | Pitfall to avoid — never an instruction to repeat |
| `incomplete` | Timed out mid-build — open listed files + TODO.md and continue |

## Not this tool

- Durable **facts** → `memory_search` / `memory_get`
- In-beat scratchpad → `working_memory_*`
- Checklist → `todo_write` / `TODO.md` (see `cross-beat-resume`)
.harness/skills/cross-beat-resume/SKILL.md25 lines 
---
name: cross-beat-resume
description: Durable TODO.md checklist protocol so a budget-killed beat resumes instead of restarting.
when_to_use: Load at beat start when TODO.md exists, when the task spans multiple beats, or when the budget warning appears. Pair with cross-beat-recall for prior beat summaries.
---

# Cross-beat resume — keep a checklist, reconcile, continue

Your worktree survives beat death. The model context does not. `TODO.md` is the durable spine.

## Protocol

1. **List the whole task up front** with `todo_write` — every step you will need, not just the current one.
2. **Check items off the moment they are done** — not at the end. A kill is abrupt.
3. **First tools every beat:** `read_file` on `TODO.md` if it exists, then reconcile against reality (`git status`, artifacts on disk, green test commands).
4. **Resume unchecked steps.** If a checked step's tests now fail, re-verify it before advancing.
5. **Never restart from scratch** when a checklist and prior work already sit in the worktree.

## Budget flush

When a tool result warns that beat budget is under 10%, call `todo_write` immediately to sync the checklist before the beat dies.

## Trust green artifacts

A step is done when its durable artifact exists and is green. Do not re-run verification "just to be sure" when you have not changed the code it covers — jump to the first checklist item whose artifact is still missing.
.harness/skills/experiment-analysis/SKILL.md58 lines 
---
name: experiment-analysis
description: How to read an A/B test or controlled experiment correctly — check the design before the result, use confidence intervals and effect sizes, resist peeking, and separate a statistically significant lift from one worth shipping. Use whenever interpreting a randomized experiment or comparing a treatment to a control.
when_to_use: Use when the evidence is a randomized experiment / A-B test / holdout — "did the variant win?", "is this lift real?", "can we ship B?". For non-randomized "did X cause Y" data, use causal-inference instead.
---

# Experiment analysis

Randomization is the strongest evidence you get for a causal claim — but only if the design is sound
and the read is honest. A "winning" variant is routinely a peeking artefact, an underpowered flip, or
a trivial lift with a tiny p-value. This skill is the discipline for reading it right.

## When NOT to use this
- The data is observational (no randomization) — use `causal-inference`.
- No control group exists — a before/after is not an experiment; treat it observationally.

## Method

### 1. Interrogate the design before the result
- **Randomization**: were units assigned at random, at the right unit (user, not session, if users
  return)? Check the arms are balanced on pre-period covariates.
- **Power**: was the sample large enough to detect the minimum effect that matters? An underpowered
  test that comes back "no significant difference" has proven nothing.
- **Sample-ratio mismatch (SRM)**: if a 50/50 split arrived 55/45, the assignment or logging is
  broken — stop and fix; the result is untrustworthy.

### 2. Read the effect, not just the p-value
Report the lift as an effect size with a **confidence interval**, absolute and relative. "B lifts
conversion by 0.4pp (95% CI 0.1–0.7pp), a +6% relative change" is a decision input; "p<0.05" is not.

### 3. Resist peeking
Repeatedly checking and stopping when it first looks significant inflates false positives massively.
Fix the horizon in advance, or use a sequential/always-valid method designed for continuous
monitoring. If someone stopped early on a peek, discount the result.

### 4. Statistical vs practical significance
With enough traffic, everything is significant. Tie the effect to the decision: is it large enough,
net of cost/risk, to ship? A significant but trivial lift is a no-ship.

### 5. Guard against experiment-specific traps
- **Novelty / primacy effects** — a shiny change spikes then fades; read a stable window.
- **Multiple metrics / variants** — testing many inflates false positives; pre-declare the primary
  metric and correct for the rest.
- **Segment mining** — "it won for mobile users in Canada" found post hoc is a hypothesis, not a result.
- **Bayesian read** — "probability B beats A" and expected loss can be a more decision-friendly framing
  than null-hypothesis testing; use it when the team reasons in those terms.

## Common failure modes
- Shipping on a peek before the planned horizon.
- Calling an underpowered null "no effect".
- Reporting significance without an effect size or interval.
- Ignoring SRM.
- Harvesting a post-hoc segment win.

## Cross-references
- `statistical-rigor` — intervals, power, multiple comparisons.
- `causal-inference` — for the non-randomized case.
- `findings-communication` — verdict, effect + interval, then the ship/no-ship call.
.harness/skills/exploratory-data-analysis/SKILL.md31 lines 
---
name: exploratory-data-analysis
description: A disciplined first pass on any new dataset before answering questions about it.
when_to_use: Use at the start of any analysis when you have a dataset (CSV, table, or warehouse) and have not yet profiled it — to understand shape, types, ranges, and data-quality issues before computing answers.
---

# Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)

Before answering any quantitative question, understand the data you have. Skipping this is how
wrong-but-confident findings happen.

## Steps

1. **Locate and load.** Find the data (`repo_search` for files, or `SELECT name FROM sqlite_master
   WHERE type='table'` for a warehouse). Load it in `notebook_run` with pandas.
2. **Profile shape and types.** Print `df.shape`, `df.dtypes`, and `df.head()`. Confirm the columns
   are the types you expect (numbers parsed as numbers, dates as dates).
3. **Check data quality.** Print `df.isna().sum()` (missing values) and `df.describe(include='all')`
   (ranges, uniques). Look for impossible values (negative counts, zero denominators) and duplicates
   (`df.duplicated().sum()`).
4. **Understand cardinality.** For categorical columns, print `df['col'].value_counts()` to see the
   groups you can split by.
5. **State assumptions.** Note any cleaning you applied (dropped rows, filled values, parsed dates)
   in your findings — a reviewer must see what you did to the data.

## Rules

- Never compute a rate with a zero or missing denominator without handling it explicitly.
- Report `n` (the number of rows) alongside any aggregate — an average over 3 rows is not the same
  claim as an average over 30,000.
- If the data contradicts the question's premise, say so rather than forcing an answer.
.harness/skills/findings-communication/SKILL.md51 lines 
---
name: findings-communication
description: How to present an analysis so a decision-maker can act on it — the Pyramid Principle (answer first, then the evidence that proves it, then caveats), quantify every claim, and name uncertainty honestly. Use when writing up any finding, recommendation, or brief.
when_to_use: Use when writing the final deliverable of any investigation — a findings doc, a recommendation, or a brief. Apply it to structure the write-up regardless of the domain.
---

# Findings communication

An analysis nobody can act on is wasted work. Decision-makers read top-down and lose patience with a
build-up. Lead with the answer; make every claim a number with a source; be honest about what you
don't know. This skill is how a distinguished analyst presents.

## When NOT to use this
- The task is a raw data dump explicitly requested as such.

## The structure (Pyramid Principle)

Answer first, reasoning second, data third — the opposite of how most drafts are written.

```
VERDICT (one sentence): what is true / what to do.
SUPPORTING FINDINGS (2–4 bullets): each is one claim + the one number that proves it + its source.
WHAT TO DO NEXT (when a decision is implied): actions ranked by impact.
CAVEATS: sample-size, measurement, and assumption limits; what would change the conclusion.
```

If you cannot write the one-sentence verdict, the analysis isn't finished — keep going, don't publish.

## Rules
- **Quantify.** Every factual claim carries the exact number you computed or found, and (for external
  facts) the source URL. "Signups rose sharply" is not a finding; "signups rose 38% (412→570/wk)" is.
- **Answer the whole question.** Address every part the task asked; a missing part fails the work.
- **Name uncertainty.** State confidence intervals, `n`, and assumptions. "I can't distinguish these
  two causes without one more slice" is a real, respectable answer; false certainty is not.
- **No process theatre.** Report the conclusion and its evidence, not a narration of which tools you
  ran. The reader wants the answer and why to believe it.
- **Self-consistency.** Numbers in the summary must match the body; dates must be real (never future);
  a ranking must agree with the figures it's built from. Re-read for contradictions before finishing.
- **Right altitude.** Give the decision-maker what changes the decision, not every intermediate table.

## Common failure modes
- Burying the answer under the methodology.
- Vague qualitative claims with no number.
- Omitting caveats, projecting false certainty.
- Summary that contradicts the body (or an impossible/future date).
- Answering some of the question and leaving parts unaddressed.

## Cross-references
- `analytics-diagnostic-method` — step 5 is this structure.
- `statistical-rigor` — the intervals and `n` that make a claim honest.
- Every other skill ends here: the deliverable is judged on how well it communicates a defensible answer.

# lattice consolidate — patterns + skill_manage (gate-gated)

Consolidation turns **recurring episodic evidence** into:

- **Patterns** — declarative facts (`api.retry`) → `lattice_apply` → `lattice_context`
- **Procedures** — playbooks → **`skill_manage(evolve|patch)`** on an existing role skill (default); `create` only for new class-level umbrellas

## Gate

1. **≥ N new beats** since last consolidation (default N = 5)
2. **A cluster** of ≥ K beats share the same file prefix or intent (default K = 2)

Silent beat-end notice → gate **closed** → do nothing.

## Preference order (Hermes-aligned)

1. **`patterns[]` via `lattice_apply`** — sticky-note facts ("client retries 429/503")
2. **`skill_manage(evolve)`** — patch a section of an existing role skill
3. **`skill_manage(create)`** — rare; class-level playbook with When to Use / Procedure / Pitfalls / Verification
4. **Nothing to save** — one-off narratives, diary entries, transient env failures

**Do NOT** put procedures in `lattice_apply` (`habits[]` is rejected). **Do NOT** capture session diaries as skills.

## Workflow (gate open only)

### 1. Packet

```
lattice_packet()
```

Habit hints suggest `suggested_action: evolve` — use `skill_manage`, not a CREATE micro-slug.

### 2. Re-read evidence

```
recall(query='retry')
get_run(run_id='run_a57d754d…')
```

Call `get_run` for every `source_run_id` you cite.

### 3. Facts → lattice_apply

```json
{
  "employee_id": "e_be_1",
  "patterns": [
    {
      "key": "api.retry",
      "claim": "The HTTP client in src/api/client.py retries 429 and 503 responses up to 3 times with exponential backoff from 0.2s to 30s.",
      "source_run_ids": ["r_done_1", "r_done_2"],
      "supersedes": null
    }
  ]
}
```

```
lattice_apply(proposal=<patterns only>)
```

### 4. Procedures → skill_manage

```
skill_manage(
  action='evolve',
  name='structuring-any-service',
  section='Before patching HTTP clients',
  content='## Before patching HTTP clients\n\n1. …\n\n## Pitfalls\n- …\n\n## Verification\n- …',
  source_run_ids=['r_done_1', 'r_done_2']
)
```

Prefer ≤10 patterns; prefer `evolve`/`patch` over `create`.

## When NOT to consolidate

- Gate closed (most beats)
- Mid-beat
- One-off / diary content — leave in episodic memory
- Sticky-note facts as skills — use `patterns[]` instead

## Tools

| Tool | Memory |
|------|--------|
| `lattice_apply` | Semantic patterns only |
| `skill_manage` | Procedural skills (versioned) |
| `lattice_context` / `skill` | Read facts / load playbooks |
